title: Two and a half per cent
word: Two and a half per cent

segments.voice: Yesterday, nisab: the line wealth must reach before zakat is owed. Now, above it, how much?

Forty dates in a bowl, counted out by hand onto a plate. Thirty-nine go back to be eaten, shared, saved. One, just one, is set apart on the edge of the plate. That's the whole share. When people first hear zakat described as a pillar of the faith, a duty beside the prayer, some expect it to be heavy. A tenth, a quarter, half. Then comes the number, and it's small. Small enough to keep doing, every year, for a whole life. One coin out of forty: two and a half percent.
screen: `FORTY DATES IN A BOWL.` → `ONE SET APART.` → `SMALLER THAN SOME EXPECT.`

segments.voice: First, the words. In Sahih al-Bukhari there's a letter Abu Bakr wrote setting out the rules of zakat, and for silver it gives the share as rub' al-'ushr. A quarter of a tenth. Take a tenth, then a quarter of that, and you have one fortieth: two and a half percent. Second, the same share in coins. A report in the Sunan of Abu Dawud has the Prophet ﷺ say to bring a quarter of a tenth, one dirham from every forty. And the threshold you met yesterday says it the same way: on two hundred dirhams, five. Two hundred divided by forty is five. The numbers in these reports agree with each other. Third, what it's charged on. Not on income as it flows in, and not on everything you own. On saved wealth above the line, held a year: cash, savings, gold and silver, goods for trade. Teachers of the law don't count your home, the clothes you wear, or the car you drive to work in the same way, and a later day looks at the categories one by one. Fourth, why such a small share might be the point. It's something a person can give every year without being ruined by it, and the people who receive it can count on it coming, year after year. Small, steady, and owed. Which is harder than it sounds. Anyone can be generous once.
screen: `A QUARTER OF A TENTH.` · `ONE DIRHAM FROM EVERY FORTY.` · `ON SAVED WEALTH ABOVE THE LINE.` · `SMALL, STEADY, OWED.` · then, large: `ONE IN FORTY.`

segments.voice: Take a round figure, your savings or any number you'd rather think about, and divide it by ten, then by four: a quarter of a tenth. Hold that number for a breath and notice how big or small it feels next to the whole. Then breathe out, and picture the thirty-nine parts that stay.
Two and a half percent. Rub' al-'ushr, a quarter of a tenth: one fortieth of saved wealth above the threshold. Today's word.
screen: `TWO AND A HALF PER CENT — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: one in forty. Small enough to keep giving, every single year. Tomorrow: the year, and how long wealth has to sit.

howItsDone: Muslims who owe zakat on money and savings give one fortieth, two and a half percent, of what they hold above the nisab, once a year, some using a mosque's or charity's zakat calculator.

chat.says: Two and a half percent of my savings? Why is the share so small?
options: One in forty is small enough to give every year, and those receiving can count on it.
Because it's only a suggestion; the real duty is a tenth of all your income.
Because it's paid every month, so it adds up to a quarter of savings a year.
chat.meaning: Abu Bakr's letter gives rub' al-'ushr, a quarter of a tenth. A share that size can be given every year, and those receiving can count on it.

rub' al-'ushr.meaning: a quarter of a tenth: one fortieth

Abu Bakr.meaning: a close companion, later the first caliph

dirham.meaning: a silver coin of the Prophet's day

Abu Dawud.meaning: the compiler of a major hadith collection, the Sunan

notes: Bukhari 1454 (Abu Bakr's letter; 'in silver, a quarter of a tenth'): confirm number and that rub' al-'ushr appears there.
Abu Dawud 1572 (bring a quarter of a tenth, one dirham from every forty): confirm number and grading.

Teach says the home, clothes and a work car are 'not counted in the same way'; that's the general position drawn from Bukhari 1463 (no sadaqah on a Muslim's horse or slave), cited on day 1098. Confirm.
